title: Can You Wash Sheets and Towels Together?

seo.title: Can You Wash Sheets and Towels Together?
seo.meta_description: Sheets and towels can share a wash when colors, temperature, and care labels are compatible, but they do not always clean best together.
seo.search_intent: Make a practical, safe decision about “Can You Wash Sheets and Towels Together,” recognize important limits, and know when to change approach or get help.

excerpt: Sheets and towels can share a wash when colors, temperature, and care labels are compatible, but they do not always clean best together. Towels are heavy, absorb a lot of water, and may shed lint; sheets can wrap around them and create a bulky load that rinses and spins poorly.
content_html:
Sheets and towels can share a wash when colors, temperature, and care labels are compatible, but they do not always clean best together. Towels are heavy, absorb a lot of water, and may shed lint; sheets can wrap around them and create a bulky load that rinses and spins poorly.

Separate new towels that still shed lint

The first washes of a towel can leave fibers on smooth sheets, especially dark ones. Wash new towels separately until shedding decreases if lint is causing a problem.

Make sure both items tolerate the same temperature

Do not raise the temperature just because towels are present when the sheets call for a gentler wash. The more sensitive care label limits the combined load and may make separation better.

Leave enough room so sheets do not wrap around everything

An overfilled load encourages large sheets to form a bundle around towels. Load the drum loosely and mix item sizes so the load can move and rinse more effectively.

Separate them if drying times are very different

Thick towels often take longer to dry than sheets. If drying together, removing sheets first prevents overdrying while towels finish, or separate them from the start to use better-matched cycles.
